page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 72 physical cores via Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance includes a 504 MB L3 cache, along with 2 MB L2 cache and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 540 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 3.75 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes instruction set support for AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and AES cryptographic primitives. The instance has no integrated local storage and no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the top tiers for parallel computing and throughput tasks. It achieves a multi-core stress-ng rating of 156,268.58 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 984.52 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 532.33 GB/sec for reads and 213.92 GB/sec for writes, contributing to high transaction capabilities including 212.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 220.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Instruction-level tests show top-tier execution in ray tracing, software compilation with Clang, and PassMark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high compute and memory density inside a single VM boundary, mitigating network overhead inherent to distributed clusters. The architectural tradeoff centers on the total lack of onboard NVMe storage, meaning data-intensive deployments must budget for and attach external persistent disks or network-attached storage. Additionally, text generation performance for larger language models remains limited by CPU execution compared to dedicated hardware accelerators.

The c4-standard-144 instance is well suited for enterprise database operations, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, in-memory caching platforms, and data engineering pipelines that require substantial thread counts alongside expansive memory buffers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 144 dedicated vCPUs and 72 physical cores running on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 540 GB of system memory (3.75 GB per vCPU) and a 504 MB L3 cache, the system incorporates instruction sets for AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic acceleration. It includes no bundled GPUs and no local storage volumes, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier multi-threaded throughput, registering 156,268.58 in multi-core stress-ng tests, 532.33 GB/sec in uncached read memory bandwidth, and 212.01 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware trade-offs include CPU-bound limits on complex text generation and dependency on remote disks. The instance fits heavy enterprise database engines, in-memory caching architectures, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
